title: Eventual equality of etale inverse-image sections
statement: Let $I$ be nonempty and directed, $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a system of qcqs schemes with affine transition morphisms, and $c$ a limit cone [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Choose $i_0\in I$, a sheaf of sets $G$ on $D(i_0)$ and a quasi-compact quasi-separated etale object $W_0$ over $D(i_0)$. Let $j,k$ be objects of $\mathrm{Over}(i_0^{\mathrm{op}})$, and $s,t$ sections of the stage inverse images on the base changes of $W_0$. If their images under the canonical cone section comparisons [def-weil-pbc-sets-section-comparison] are equal, there are a common later object $l$ and arrows $a:l\to j$, $b:l\to k$ such that the transition comparisons map $s$ and $t$ to equal sections at $l$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), degree zero for sheaves of sets; proof via Tags 0EYL, 04HR, 09YN and the finite affine-cover reduction for qcqs schemes

proof.text: Choose the finite affine family of etale_finite_affine_restriction_detection. Restrict the two sections to each affine member. Restriction naturality transports the assumed cone equality to the restricted sections, so affine eventual equality gives a later stage and two arrows for each member.

Use IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists on the finite set containing j, k, and all local witness stages, choosing arrows from l to every stage. Hom sets in Over of a preorder are subsingletons, so composites through each local stage equal the chosen arrows to j and k. Apply the comparison composition laws to transport every local equality to l. Restriction naturality then identifies these with restrictions of the two global sections. The finite affine restriction detection theorem gives their equality. Including j and k in the finite set handles an empty family without a separate inhabitedness assumption.
